papers.title: Winning Arguments: Interaction Dynamics and Persuasion Strategies in Good-faith Online Discussions
papers.study_kind: observational corpus analysis and predictive modelling
papers.scope: Read all 12 recovered PDF pages including appendix and references; online CMV written interactions, invited challenge audience and original poster as recipient.
papers.sample_and_design: Temporal training/heldout discussion trees; matched positive and negative rooted path units from same original post and most similar root content-word Jaccard; separate OP outcome task. See findings for denominators.
outcomes: OP-awarded delta as immediate participant-reported change in view, not truth, comprehension, enduring belief or behavior

findings.claim: Training 18,363 and heldout 2,263 discussion trees; 1,114,533 and 145,733 nodes respectively.
findings.denominator: Discussion trees and nodes separately; 2013-01-01 to 2015-05-07 versus 2015-05-08 to 2015-09-01
findings.interpretation_limits: Archive counts, not independent selected pairs.

findings.denominator: pairs, one delta winning and one unsuccessful, within same OP and lexically similar
findings.interpretation_limits: At least 10 challengers, three unsuccessful paths before OP last reply, each root at least 50 words; matching does not equate content or exposure.
Pair classification, not proportion persuaded or causal effects; full-path uses later dialogue.

findings.claim: Equal-length dissection truncates longer reply after lexical matching.
findings.interpretation_limits: It removes material, can change distributions and reverse signs; non-significance does not establish no effect.

findings.claim: Hedges and first/second-person pronouns are higher in raw counts in winning replies; no T indicator in Table 3.
findings.denominator: selected matched winning and unsuccessful root replies and full paths
findings.interpretation_limits: Length-associated counts; no evidence a hedge or pronoun edit causes persuasion.

findings.claim: Definite and indefinite raw article counts track length; definite-article fraction retained significance in truncated roots.
findings.denominator: selected pairs; adjusted by Bonferroni in training comparisons
findings.interpretation_limits: Ratio is not a prescription to substitute articles; specificity interpretation is authors inference.

findings.claim: Among long paths, zero of 129 with six or more challenger replies and one of approximately 3,000 with five received a delta.
findings.denominator: paths classified by challenger reply count
findings.interpretation_limits: Observational selection and engagement confounding; not a causal cutoff.

findings.claim: 10,743 train and 1,529 heldout original posts; heldout AUC approximately 0.54.
findings.denominator: selected OPs with at least ten challengers and at least one OP reply
findings.interpretation_limits: Weak outcome prediction; delta not personality trait or comprehension.

findings.claim: First-person pronouns and first-person plural in original posts showed opposite associations with delta.
findings.denominator: selected OP task training set, Bonferroni-corrected comparisons
findings.interpretation_limits: Authors self-affirmation explanation speculative and prior work cited in opposite direction; different from reply pronoun raw counts.

findings.claim: No significant concreteness or dominance difference in replies; root Flesch-Kincaid not significant, full-path difference significant.
findings.interpretation_limits: Null comparisons are not proof of equivalence; full-path observations include later dialogue.

findings.claim: Number of challengers and delta fraction increased sublinearly; in subtrees with two to four replies, single-challenger performed better.
findings.denominator: discussion trees binned by number of challengers; subtrees stratified by 2–4 replies
findings.interpretation_limits: Selection and differences in argument difficulty confound interpretations.

findings.claim: Topic-model features did not improve prediction; discourse-connector sequences performed poorly.

limitations: No randomization; timing, visibility, author selection and interaction confounded. Authors explicitly disclaim causal explanations p. 2.
Lexical matching does not isolate reasoning, evidence or claim truth. Truncation removes text.
Self-selected moderated CMV community is not general reader population.
Full-path predictors may be subsequent to opening reply; no prospective editing benefit established.

rule_implications.trigger: Author requests response to known viewpoint
rule_implications.benefit: Retain audience and specific claim context for author review
rule_implications.mechanical: Store supplied claim, audience and source target separately
rule_implications.semantic: Judge whether reply engages claim fairly and appropriately
rule_implications.counterexample: Personal exploration without a known opposing claim needs no opponent record

rule_implications.trigger: Uncertainty or qualification changes claim meaning
rule_implications.semantic: Judge whether qualifier is warranted and what it scopes
rule_implications.counterexample: Redundant hedges can obscure a fact; necessary may can prevent false certainty
rule_implications.evidence: P02 Table 3 pp. 6, 10 raw counts do not isolate effect

rule_implications.trigger: Context contains speakers, reply edges and targets
rule_implications.benefit: Keep author, addressee and referenced claim distinguishable
rule_implications.mechanical: Preserve source-provided IDs, reply edge, spans and unknowns
rule_implications.semantic: Determine actual actor, addressee, function and relation target in context
rule_implications.counterexample: Quoted you addresses a character rather than the reader
rule_implications.evidence: P02 pp. 3–6; reply edge is not function gold

rule_implications.trigger: An automatic system proposes optimizing delta proxy
rule_implications.benefit: Protect author intent, evidence, voice and semantic accuracy
rule_implications.mechanical: Retain count as descriptive only if task relevant
rule_implications.semantic: Assess whether words, links and emphasis serve actual intent
rule_implications.counterexample: Technical explanation must preserve a term; safety warning may require urgency

papers.extraction_issues: Original p613.pdf streams corrupt; two extractors yield blank PDF pages 1 and 4. Official Cornell author copy recovered; source hash and location in experiments/evidence-integration-2026-11-16/P02-recovery.json; all recovered pages reviewed.

cross_paper_synthesis: One-paper review; no pooled or cross-paper statistical synthesis.
Fresh local calibration was 21/36 original and 18/36 revised exact-set agreement; no semantic gold, no demonstrated improvement, no full realization spans. P02 does not validate those rules.
Audience-aware provenance and structured reply relationships are common infrastructure; author-controlled alternatives might be useful but an advantage is unmeasured.

github_reuse.name: Cornell original dataset and author walkthrough
github_reuse.reuse: Review documented JSONL pair, OP and discussion schema; walkthrough preprocessing is explicitly simplified and not full replication.
github_reuse.limits: 321 MB archive not downloaded; code/data/Reddit rights to be separately checked.

github_reuse.name: ConvoKit Winning Arguments conversion
github_reuse.reuse: Schema for speaker, timestamp, reply_to, conversation, success and pair_ids; preserve source release and values.
github_reuse.limits: 3,051 conversations, 293,297 utterances, 34,911 speakers per subset documentation; 530 missing author/text. Reused pairs are clustered; null success is not failure. Rights and notebook execution unverified.

open_questions: How should target and audience be represented when inferred, unknown, or quoted rather than explicitly supplied?
Would author-controlled contextual prompts improve real reader or author outcomes in fresh, grouped evaluation?
Can original preprocessing and dependency versions be reconstructed under available rights without reusing overlapping pairs across evaluation splits?
